newsitem.title: JAPAN: Ok Tedi copper delivery to Japan delayed -- smelter.
newsitem.headline: Ok Tedi copper delivery to Japan delayed -- smelter.

text.p: Nippon Mining and Metals Co, Japan's largest copper smelter, said on Thursday that June copper delivery from the Ok Tedi mine in Papua New Guinea has been delayed due to dry river conditions.

A Nippon Mining official told Reuters that officials from the Ok Tedi copper mine came to Japan earlier this week to inform the company that they had not been able to deliver concentrates to port because of dry river conditions.
"They said they could deliver the concentrates by the end of June, if it rains now," she said. "Everything depends on the weather."
The Nippon Mining official said Japan's smelters import 230,000 tonnes of copper concentrates a year from the Ok Tedi mine, or some 25,000 tonnes a month.

Asked if smelters would need to acquire copper concentrates somewhere else, the official said: "The situation must be different in each company, but we are not thinking of buying other concentrates at the moment."
She said there were no problems with the May shipments.
Ok Tedi is 52.6 percent owned by Australia's Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, with Canada's Inmet Mining Corp owning 17.4 percent and the rest held by the Papua New Guinea government.
